 Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra
Order Order
 No. 05.10.2024
 03. 1.

This is an application under Section-439 Cr.P.C.
2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. The petitioner is an accused in connection with Jeypore Mahila P.S. Case No.34 of 2024 c o r r e s p o n d i n g t o G . R . C a s e N o .

2 5 3 o f 2 0 2 4 f o r t h e o f f e n c e s u n d e r Sections-376(2)(n)/376(3)/294/506 of the IPC read with Sections 4(2) & 6 of the POCSO Act pending in the Court of the learned A.S.J.-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Jeypore.
The petitioner had moved an application before the Court of learned trial Court for grant of bail.
The learned trial Court vide order dated 24.05.2024 rejected his application.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the plea of bail of the petitioner is not pending before any other Court except the present one.

5. The prosecution case is that since five years while the complainant was about 15 years old, one Sunil Pujari of her village was keeping physical relationship with her with the assurance of marring her.
She further alleged that the accused used to always came to her house in late night and by assaulting her sexually and used to abuse her in obscene languages.
She narrated those things to her parents and village gentries.
The village gentries along with her family members called a meeting but the accused denied to marry her.

Hence, the F.I.R.
6.
The victim has been examined as P.W.1.

In her cross-examination, she has stated as under:

1 "27.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a fact that I was in love relationship with A1 from my side also and I wanted to marry him and that I have lodged this case against A1 out of anger due to refusal by the family members of A1 for my marriage with A1."
Perusal of the evidence indicates that the petitioner has been relationship with the victim.
Since there was assurance of marriage, they had kept physical relationship.
This aspect is also narrated in the statements of the witnesses examined under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
The petitioner is aged about 29 years and the victim is aged about 23 years now.

From the evidence on record, nature of accusation and age of both the victim & accused, it can be inferred that this is neither a case of perpetration of sexual exploitation or abuse nor emotional obtrude caused to the vulnerable girl,rather it was a love affair went sour.
Therefore, the accused is entitled to bail.
7. Regard being had to the period of custody of the petitioner from 21.05.2024 and the nature of accusation, age of the petitioner, I am inclined to admit the petitioner to bail.

Hence, the petitioner be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper subject to further conditions as following:
(i) The petitioner shall cooperate with the investigation,
(ii) He shall not tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever,
(iii) He shall not contact with the victim or her family members, and (iv) He shall not involve in any similar type of offence.
Violation of any conditions of bail shall entail consideration for cancellation of the bail granted to the petitioner.
The prosecution is given liberty to move an application for cancellation of bail before the Court below, if the petitioner violates any conditions of the bail granted to him.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.

(S.S. Mishra) Judge amit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Sunil Pujari vs State Of Odisha & Another .... Opp. ... on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178763674/
